Bottom line:
China's April activity data are scheduled for release next Monday (18 May). We expect industrial production (IP) growth to rebound to
yoy in April from

yoy in March, as stronger-than-expected exports, a narrower year-on-year contraction in steel demand, and an improvement in automobile output growth indicate modestly better manufacturing sector momentum despite the global energy-supply shock. We expect year-on-year fixed asset investment (FAI) growth to slow further to
in April from

in March on a single-month basis, reflecting a dip in the NBS construction PMI, a notable contraction in policy bank net financing and heavy rainfalls in southern China. Our forecast implies year-to-date FAI growth would be
yoy in April. Retail sales growth may rise slightly to
yoy in April from

yoy in March, as higher energy prices may have boosted gasoline sales value growth and the nationwide promotion of spring breaks this year may have frontloaded some dining-out demand to April from May, despite still-subdued automobile and home appliance sales growth. Our April activity data forecasts are slightly above market consensus for IP, largely in line for retail sales, but slightly below for FAI.
